title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
summary: Version 1.7.1 reduces CPU overhead during active editing by debouncing decoration scans and caching per-document symbol lookups in semantic highlighting.

highlights.title: Debounced decoration scans
highlights.description: Null-assertion highlighting, hex color swatches, and string resource folding no longer re-scan the entire document on every keystroke — rapid typing stays smooth.

highlights.title: Semantic token cache
highlights.description: Symbols that appear multiple times in the same file are now resolved once and reused, cutting redundant work in semantic highlighting for large Kotlin files.

highlights.title: Expanded test coverage
highlights.description: Adversarial and performance test suites were added for three decoration providers and semantic tokens, directly increasing confidence that visual features stay correct under malformed or edge-case inputs.

sections.heading: Performance
bullets: Debounced keystroke-driven scans in NullAssertionProvider, HexColorFoldingProvider, and StringResourceFoldingProvider — rapid typing no longer triggers a full document scan on every character.
Added a per-document word cache in SemanticTokensProvider so symbols that appear multiple times in the same file are resolved only once per render pass.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: No new commands, settings, or navigation features in this release — all changes are performance and reliability improvements to existing visual annotations.
Adversarial and performance test suites were added for the affected providers, increasing confidence that decoration and semantic highlighting remain correct under edge conditions.
